applied.problem: "Past 0.6 leading ... the output must pass 115 V" is not literally true: with the drop pointing just behind square the output is still a hair under 115 V; at full load it crosses 115 V only near 0.58 leading (cos α = −d/230), so it passes 115 V a little further on.

Screen 6 repeats the claim that once the drop points back the output must pass 115 V (it crosses only near 0.58 leading at full load); screen 13's why says the 8% drop is exactly twice and the fault current exactly half, true only for the same resistance-to-reactance mix and a stiff supply.

Read alone, "draws up to 1739 A" and "halve the impedance and the fault current doubles" overstate: a plate impedance carries a tolerance and a supply can run above nominal, while a real supply's impedance makes halving Z% less than double the current; both are stiff-supply terminal figures.
